start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:find-anything-across-my-rows with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and query \"harbour boats\"." It finds the things in your own rows that mention both words and tells you where each one opens.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: the searchable rows are the person's own, in whatever form their store keeps them, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the searchable rows are kept and how the store is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:find-anything-across-my-rows" with store and the query.
3. The first run makes the search rows once and proves the search on the example rows: every expected answer must match, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run lists the things that have every word of the query, highest rank first, each with the address that opens it.

worked_examples.title: Find the harbour things

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the example rows kept in the person's database; the prove step matched every expected answer.
worked_examples.hands_back: Three things, highest rank first: "doc:harbour" with rank 3, "note:7" with rank 2 and "rec:talk-1" with rank 2.

worked_examples.title: A search with no words is refused

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "refused" with the reason that a search needs at least one word; nothing is searched.
